state.terms_of_service:
Standard Personal Account Terms (excerpt for evaluation noise). This text is not a live contract.

1. The account is a stored-value account for personal use. Business activity, resale of access, and operating as a money transmitter for third parties are outside the permitted use.

2. Eligibility. You must be old enough to hold an account in your country of residence, pass identity checks, and keep a reachable email and phone number. We may ask again for documents if risk signals change.

3. Opening and refusal. We may refuse an application without giving a reason required by financial-crime law. If we open an account, we may still limit features until source-of-funds checks finish.

4. Safeguards. Funds are safeguarded with partner institutions according to applicable e-money rules. Safeguarding is not a deposit guarantee scheme and does not make the balance a bank deposit unless a separate bank partner product says so.

5. Cards. Physical and virtual cards remain our property. You must sign, activate, and keep the PIN secret. Contactless, magnetic stripe, and chip use may have different merchant and country limits.

6. Card replacement. Worn, expiring, lost, stolen, or swallowed cards can be replaced. Delivery times vary by country and postal partner. A replacement may use a new PAN. Disposable virtual cards are one-time numbers and are not posted.

7. Wallets. Adding a card to Apple Pay or Google Pay is optional and follows the wallet provider rules. Tokenised payments are still card payments under these terms.

8. ATM cash. Cash withdrawals may incur a fee, a foreign-exchange margin, or both. Some ATMs charge their own operator fee which we do not control. If an ATM dispenses the wrong amount, report it promptly with the receipt.

9. Transfers. Outbound transfers can be cancelled only while they are still pending in our system. Once released to the scheme, recall is best-effort and may fail. Recipients who do not receive funds must be distinguished from delays in your own inbound credit.

10. Beneficiaries. We may block payees in sanctioned regions, high-risk categories, or after fraud reports. A blocked beneficiary is not a failed transfer of a permitted payee.

11. Top-ups. You may add money by card, bank transfer, cash, or cheque where offered. Automatic top-up triggers when the balance falls below a threshold you set. Top-up limits can be daily, rolling, or lifetime. A verification charge may appear before a card top-up completes.

12. Failed versus reversed top-ups. A failed top-up never credited the balance. A reverted top-up credited and was later taken back, often after a chargeback or suspected fraud.

13. Fees. Fees may apply to card payments, ATM withdrawals, transfers, currency conversion, and some top-up rails. The fee schedule is published in the app. An extra statement line that is not in the schedule should be queried as an unrecognised charge.

14. Foreign exchange. The displayed mid-market rate is indicative. The booked rate on a card payment, ATM withdrawal, or in-app conversion may include a margin. Weekend and offshore rates can differ.

15. Direct debits and repeating payments. You authorise merchants separately. Unrecognised direct debits can be claimed under the scheme rules. Chargebacks on card purchases follow the card scheme, not the direct-debit scheme.

16. Refunds. A merchant refund is not instant. It can take several business days after the merchant posts it. Requesting a new refund is different from chasing a refund already issued.

17. Pending authorisations. Card holds reduce available funds before settlement. Pending ATM withdrawals and pending transfers are separate states. A pending item that never settles should drop off; remaining holds should be reported.

18. Declines. We may decline a card payment, ATM withdrawal, or transfer for insufficient funds, suspected fraud, merchant category blocks, or scheme errors. A decline is not a settled charge.

19. Duplicate charges. If the same merchant reference posts twice, one entry may drop after clearing. Keep receipts until the statement confirms a single amount.

20. Identity. We may ask you to verify identity, explain source of funds, or confirm a top-up. Refusing required checks can freeze outbound payments. Completing a check is not the same as asking why the check exists.

21. Security. Lost phones, stolen cards, and leaked PANs are different incidents. Freeze the app from another device if the phone is gone. Report a missing card even if you later find it.

22. PIN and passcode. Too many wrong PIN tries can block the chip. An app passcode is not the card PIN. Reset paths differ and may require identity checks.

23. Countries. Availability of accounts, cards, ATM cash, and local rails depends on residence and travel location. Some features are off in listed countries.

24. Age and additional cards. Younger users may have reduced features. A spare card for another person on the same account, if offered, remains your responsibility.

25. Closing. You may request account termination after settling negative balances and destroying cards. We may also close an account for risk, inactivity, or legal duty. Remaining funds are returned to a named account in your name where law allows.

26. Statements and notices. We send notices to the email on file. You must keep personal details current. Support hours in the app are not a promise of 24-hour human coverage.

27. Liability. Unauthorised payments reported quickly may be refunded under applicable rules. Gross negligence, sharing PINs, or delayed reporting can reduce that protection. ATM operator faults are handled with the operator.

28. Changes. We may change fees, limits, and these terms with notice in the app. Continued use after the effective date is acceptance except where local law requires an opt-in.

29. Complaints. Start with in-app support. If unresolved, you may escalate to the named ombudsman or regulator for your residence. Escalation does not freeze fraud-prevention holds.

30. Language. If translations differ, the English excerpt is for this evaluation only and is not the governing legal text of a live product.

Appendix A. Example fee names that may appear: card payment fee, ATM fee, transfer fee, FX conversion fee, card top-up fee, bank-transfer top-up fee. Names on a live statement may differ.

Appendix B. Example timelines. Card post 5-10 working days inland, longer overseas. Bank transfers may show as pending the same day and credit the recipient later. Merchant refunds often 3-10 working days after the merchant action.

Appendix C. Records. We keep logs of logins, device changes, failed PIN tries, and support chats for security and complaints. Login history in the app may be incomplete for old devices.

Appendix D. Third parties. Card schemes, ATM owners, correspondent banks, wallet providers, and postal carriers have their own terms. Failures at those parties can look like failures in the app.

Appendix E. Prohibited activity includes fraud, sanctioned counterparties, and abuse of chargebacks. We may share information with schemes and law enforcement as required.

Appendix F. Virtual cards. Reusable virtual cards keep a stable number until replaced. Disposable virtual cards rotate. Limits on disposable cards are separate from the physical card limit.

Appendix G. Support. Written support may quote these sections. Quoting a section does not decide a specific dispute about a fee, decline, or missing transfer.

Appendix noise 01. Operational note for agents: unused product flags, legacy BIN ranges, weekend FX windows, and postal exception codes are stored for audit and are not required to classify a customer's latest message. This paragraph exists to enlarge state for the context-rot condition.

intent.instructions: Which intent best matches the customer's request in `query`?

card_arrival.what: The customer is waiting for a physical card that was already ordered and asks if it has arrived or where it is
card_arrival.not_for: Asking how long delivery usually takes before or without tracking a specific order
examples: My new card still has not shown up

criteria.card_linking: The customer wants to attach an existing physical or virtual card to the app or account
criteria.exchange_rate: The customer wants the current foreign-exchange rate, not a fee already charged
criteria.card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate: A completed card purchase used a worse exchange rate than the customer expected
criteria.extra_charge_on_statement: An unexplained extra line appears on the statement and is not identified as a known fee type

pending_cash_withdrawal.what: An ATM or cash withdrawal is still pending
pending_cash_withdrawal.not_for: A pending card purchase or pending transfer
examples: My ATM withdrawal is still pending

criteria.fiat_currency_support: The customer asks which government-issued currencies the product supports

card_delivery_estimate.what: The customer wants the usual or promised delivery time for a card, not the status of a specific shipment
card_delivery_estimate.not_for: Chasing a card that should already have arrived
examples: How many days does a new card usually take to arrive?

criteria.automatic_top_up: The customer wants to set, change, or stop automatic top-ups when the balance is low
criteria.card_not_working: The card fails in general use and the cause is not a specific decline, ATM swallow, or contactless fault
criteria.exchange_via_app: The customer wants to convert currency inside the app

lost_or_stolen_card.what: The physical card is missing, stolen, or the customer cannot find it and needs it blocked or replaced
lost_or_stolen_card.not_for: Fraud on a card the customer still has, or a phone that was lost
examples: I think someone stole my card

criteria.age_limit: The customer asks the minimum age to open or use the account or card
criteria.pin_blocked: The PIN is locked after wrong attempts and the customer cannot use it
criteria.contactless_not_working: Contactless tap-to-pay fails while other card uses may still work
criteria.top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge: A fee was added when topping up by bank transfer
criteria.pending_top_up: A top-up is still processing and has not credited yet
criteria.cancel_transfer: The customer wants to stop an outbound transfer that has not finished
criteria.top_up_limits: The customer asks how much they can top up, or has hit a top-up cap
criteria.wrong_amount_of_cash_received: The ATM dispensed a different amount of cash than was charged

card_payment_fee_charged.what: A fee was added to a card payment the customer made
card_payment_fee_charged.not_for: Fees on cash withdrawals, bank transfers, or top-ups
examples: Why was I charged extra for paying by card?

transfer_not_received_by_recipient.what: The customer sent money and the recipient says it never arrived
transfer_not_received_by_recipient.not_for: The sender's own balance not updating after an inbound transfer
examples: The person I paid did not get the money

criteria.supported_cards_and_currencies: The customer asks which card schemes or currencies can be used
criteria.getting_virtual_card: The customer wants a reusable virtual card number, not a disposable one and not a physical card
criteria.card_acceptance: The customer asks where the card can be used, or a merchant will not take it

top_up_reverted.what: A top-up that had succeeded was later undone and the money taken back
top_up_reverted.not_for: A top-up that never completed in the first place
examples: You reversed a top-up that had already landed

criteria.balance_not_updated_after_cheque_or_cash: A cheque or cash deposit has not appeared on the balance
criteria.card_payment_not_recognised: A card purchase the customer does not recognise appears on the account
criteria.edit_personal_details: The customer wants to change name, address, email, or other profile data

why_verify_identity.what: The customer asks why the bank is requesting identity checks
why_verify_identity.not_for: Wanting to start or finish the verification steps
examples: Why do you need my passport?

criteria.unable_to_verify_identity: Identity verification was attempted and failed or cannot be completed
criteria.get_physical_card: The customer asks how to obtain a physical card they do not yet have, including first-time issue
criteria.visa_or_mastercard: The customer asks whether the card is Visa or Mastercard, or wants a specific scheme
criteria.topping_up_by_card: The customer wants to add money using a debit or credit card
criteria.disposable_card_limits: The customer asks spending or count limits that apply to disposable virtual cards

compromised_card.what: The customer still has the card but suspects the details were stolen or used without permission
compromised_card.not_for: A card that is physically lost or stolen
examples: Someone knows my card number and used it

criteria.atm_support: The customer asks which ATMs work, or whether cash withdrawal is supported
criteria.direct_debit_payment_not_recognised: A direct debit the customer does not recognise was taken
criteria.passcode_forgotten: The customer cannot remember the app passcode or login code

declined_cash_withdrawal.what: An ATM or cash withdrawal was declined
declined_cash_withdrawal.not_for: A declined card purchase or declined transfer

pending_card_payment.what: A card purchase is still pending and has not settled
pending_card_payment.not_for: A pending ATM withdrawal or a pending outbound transfer
examples: Why is this card purchase still pending?

criteria.lost_or_stolen_phone: The phone used with the app was lost or stolen, not the payment card

request_refund.what: The customer wants the bank to start a refund or chargeback
request_refund.not_for: A refund that was already promised but has not appeared

Refund_not_showing_up.what: A refund the customer expects is missing from the balance or statement
Refund_not_showing_up.not_for: Asking to start a new refund
examples: The merchant refunded me but I do not see it

declined_card_payment.what: A card purchase was declined at a merchant
declined_card_payment.not_for: A declined ATM withdrawal or a declined transfer
examples: My card was declined in a shop

criteria.pending_transfer: An outbound transfer is still processing
criteria.terminate_account: The customer wants to close the account permanently
criteria.card_swallowed: An ATM kept or captured the physical card
criteria.transaction_charged_twice: The same payment appears more than once
criteria.verify_source_of_funds: The bank asked where the customer's money came from and the customer is responding to that check
criteria.transfer_timing: The customer asks how long a transfer takes in general, not about one missing payment
criteria.reverted_card_payment?: A card payment that had gone through was later reversed
criteria.change_pin: The customer wants to set or replace the card PIN, and the PIN is not blocked
criteria.beneficiary_not_allowed: The payee is blocked or not permitted for transfers

transfer_fee_charged.what: A fee was added when the customer sent money to someone
transfer_fee_charged.not_for: Fees on card purchases or ATM withdrawals
examples: Why did sending money cost extra?

criteria.receiving_money: The customer wants to know how others can pay them, or is expecting inbound funds
criteria.failed_transfer: An outbound transfer did not complete
criteria.transfer_into_account: The customer wants to move money into this account from another of their accounts
criteria.verify_top_up: The customer must confirm a top-up (for example a verification charge) before it completes
criteria.getting_spare_card: The customer wants an extra physical card on the same account, such as for a partner
criteria.top_up_by_cash_or_cheque: The customer wants to add money with cash or a cheque
criteria.order_physical_card: The customer wants to place an order for a physical card, including a replacement order
criteria.virtual_card_not_working: A virtual card number is failing in use
criteria.wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal: An ATM withdrawal used a worse exchange rate than expected
criteria.get_disposable_virtual_card: The customer wants a single-use virtual card, not a reusable virtual card

top_up_failed.what: A top-up attempt did not complete and the money was not added
top_up_failed.not_for: A top-up that completed and was later reversed
examples: My top-up did not go through

balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer.what: An inbound bank transfer should have credited the customer's own balance but has not
balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer.not_for: An outbound payment the recipient did not receive
examples: I sent money from my other bank and my balance here did not change

criteria.cash_withdrawal_not_recognised: An ATM or cash withdrawal the customer does not recognise appears on the account
criteria.exchange_charge: A fee was added for converting currency
criteria.top_up_by_card_charge: A fee was added when topping up by card
criteria.activate_my_card: The customer wants an already received card turned on so it can be used

cash_withdrawal_charge.what: A fee was added to an ATM or cash withdrawal
cash_withdrawal_charge.not_for: Fees on card purchases or on sending a transfer
examples: The ATM charged me a fee

criteria.card_about_to_expire: The card expiry date is near and the customer asks about renewal or a replacement before expiry
criteria.apple_pay_or_google_pay: The customer wants to add the card to Apple Pay or Google Pay, or asks if those wallets are supported

verify_my_identity.what: The customer wants to complete identity verification or asks how to pass KYC
verify_my_identity.not_for: Asking why verification is required, or reporting that verification failed
examples: How do I verify my identity?

criteria.country_support: The customer asks whether the product works in a country, for travel, or for residents of a place
